title: Containment warroom handoff and stability roadmap - Crestline Logistics
summary: Short bridge to hand back to ops: we reviewed the immediate containment steps taken by Crestline, walked through Redwood's preliminary RCA (likely KV cache thrash + hot-path batching misalignment), agreed on short-term mitigations (rate‑limit and fallback routing), and committed to a joint load test, runbook handoff, and a canary rollout plan. Security/scoping questions (audit logs, KMS) to be answered via follow-up doc.
action_items: Ethan Park - publish draft stabilization runbook and steps for hot-path throttling by 2026-01-25
Priya Shah - share cost/throughput tradeoff spreadsheet and dedicated capacity options by 2026-01-22
Marta Ruiz - provide sample traffic profiles and SLO targets by 2026-01-20
David Chen - confirm internal stakeholder list and procurement timeline by 2026-01-23
Ethan Park & Crestline SREs - schedule joint load test (50k requests/min sim) week of Jan 26 (tentative)
Priya Shah - attach Redwood security package and SOC2 summary to CRM record by 2026-01-19
next_steps: Run joint load test and collect latency/cold-start KPIs
Exchange runbook and postmortem doc for alignment
Canary a fallback model route for 24-48 hours with 10% traffic
Confirm procurement path if Dedicated capacity is chosen
Follow up on KMS integration feasibility for Crestline's Private deployment
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-18
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Priya Shah (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (Crestline SRE), David Chen (Crestline CTO), Liam O'Neill (Crestline Head of Platform)

Auto-summary: quick handoff from warroom into stabilization planning; focus on root cause, short term mitigations, and next 2 weeks of runbook + tests.

[00:00:05] Priya (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining on short notice. I know this was kind of a late warroom exit, um, so we wanted to hand over, make sure the ops steps are clear, and map next actions. Ethan is gonna walk through what we saw.

[00:00:28] Ethan (SE): Yeah hi, hi. Quick context — thanks Marta and David for the quick recap earlier. So what we observed from traces: a burst of requests to the embedding endpoint plus a correlated spike in prefix cache evictions - so my working hypo is the KV cache thrash on hot keys while batching latency grew, which pushed long tail tokens over S L A. There was also a small misconfiguration in the autoscaler threshold — it didn't trigger early, so pools were starved.

[00:01:05] Marta (SRE): Mm hm - correct - that's what we saw. The redis layer, sorry the in‑memory prefix store, started evicting earlier than expected when we had the 2 big jobs kick off. There might be a pattern with those jobs and specific customer ids.

[00:01:22] David (CTO): Are you sure it's the cache and not some, I dunno, connection leak in the serving runtime? We had a couple of ephemeral errors — timeouts — that looked different.

[00:01:36] Ethan (SE): Good call — we looked at the connection churn metrics and there was a modest increase but not sustained. The traces point to longer per-token compute time once the KV lookups started missing, so compute + queueing explains the tail. Could be multi-factor, but cache thrash is the dominant signal.

[00:02:10] Priya (AE): For the customer record — high level: root cause proto is cache eviction + autoscale threshold alignment. Impact: 20‑minute degradation window with 5–8x increase in p95 tail latency, leading to retries and visible user errors.

[00:03:05] Liam (Head of Platform): We rolled a temporary rule to route non‑critical traffic to the lower‑cost model and capped requests per minute for the hotspot API, that seemed to bring error rates down. Question — what are the tradeoffs if we keep that rule?

[00:03:25] Ethan (SE): Tradeoffs: you'd see slightly different output quality from fallback model (we observed ~1.7% change on our eval prompts), but cost drops ~22% and tail latency improves to baseline. Also you reduce pressure on prefix/KV cache, so fewer evictions.

[00:04:00] Marta (SRE): One more note — when we toggled prefix cache size up, there was a small memory bump but it did stop immediate evictions. We do have headroom for an increase but not arbitrarily.

[00:04:28] David (CTO): Okay we need a concrete stabilization plan that ops can run without going into another warroom. What does that look like?

[00:04:45] Ethan (SE): Short term immediate steps (what we recommend now): 1) Apply a 10% canary redirect to fallback model for user-facing non‑critical traffic for 24–48 hours; 2) Lower the autoscaler threshold to trigger earlier (we provided a suggested delta in the doc); 3) Apply request rate‑limits on hotspot endpoints to cap injection from background jobs; 4) Increase prefix cache reserved size by X (we'll give exact numbers after you share traffic profile).

[00:05:30] Priya (AE): We'll put all that into a one‑page runbook and hand it to Marta's team for execution — Ethan, can you own the draft?

[00:05:42] Ethan (SE): Yep I'll own. Plan to push a draft by Jan 25.

[00:06:05] Marta (SRE): Sounds good. Also, can we get a reproducible test (load script) so we can run the same pattern in staging?

[00:06:18] Ethan (SE): Absolutely — we'll assemble a k6 script and a small harness that simulates the mixed workload — batch jobs + user traffic. We'll include the payload patterns and token distributions.

[00:06:40] Priya (AE): On the procurement/security side, David — I know you flagged KMS and audit log retention as blockers for Private deployment. We have a security bundle, can share now, but there will be follow-up Qs.

[00:06:55] David (CTO): Yeah we need to ensure the HSM/KMS flow plugs into our existing vault and that audit logs meet retention 1 year minimum for our regulators. Also SSO mapping and RBAC for service accounts.

[00:07:15] Priya (AE): Noted — I'll attach SOC2 summary and the KMS integration doc to the CRM today.

[00:07:30] Liam (Head of Platform): How much does switching to Dedicated capacity buy us here versus tuning hosted settings?

[00:07:44] Ethan (SE): Dedicated gives you predictable capacity and reduces noisy neighbor risk — you can pin a model variant and tune kernel parameters more aggressively. For this particular failure mode, Dedicated would reduce interference and let you reserve larger KV cache state, but it's not a silver bullet if autoscaling thresholds and traffic shaping aren't addressed. We'll send a cost/benefit spreadsheet.

[00:08:20] Marta (SRE): There's also a question about lead time — if we go Dedicated what is the earliest you can provision a pool for us?

[00:08:29] Priya (AE): Typical lead is 4–6 weeks for reserved capacity, but we can look at short term burst options and rapid pilot capacity — I'll put options in the doc.

[00:09:05] David (CTO): Ok, let's talk mitigation timeline. Ideally we want the joint load test and the runbook in place next week. Can we do that?

[00:09:18] Ethan (SE): Week of Jan 26 is doable for the 50k rps sim but we need your traffic profile and a staging window. Marta, can you provide sample profiles by Jan 20?

[00:09:33] Marta (SRE): Yes, we'll share a CSV and the cron job schedule.

[00:09:45] Priya (AE): Let's capture risks — if the canary causes user-visible regressions we'll roll it back within 1 hour and route back to primary. If tail latency persists, we escalate to a limited traffic freeze on background jobs.

[00:10:15] Liam (Head of Platform): Any regulatory concerns with routing to fallback models? Some of our requests touch PHI-ish fields, so we'd need to ensure the fallback path preserves redaction and retention controls.

[00:10:30] Ethan (SE): Good point — avoid sending PHI to any non‑audited endpoints. We can configure the routing policy to exclude specific endpoints and apply data redaction tokenization at the gateway. We'll include recommended policies in the runbook.

[00:11:05] Marta (SRE): For telemetry, we need per‑token latency histograms and the ability to slice by prefix/key. Does Redwood expose that in the console or do we need tracing hooks?

[00:11:20] Ethan (SE): You get per‑token breakdowns in the console and we can add trace headers so you can correlate with your tracing system. There are a few caveats — sometimes the agent drops the KV key name in pseudonymized logs, so we'll walk through mapping.

[00:12:10] David (CTO): How do we keep confidence up with our exec team? They want a postmortem and a 90‑day mitigation plan.

[00:12:24] Priya (AE): We'll produce a lightweight postmortem that captures timeline, impact, root cause hypothesis, mitigations, and a 90‑day roadmap — we'll preview it with you before sending to execs.

[00:12:40] Liam (Head of Platform): Who signs off on the postmortem?

[00:12:45] David (CTO): I will, after we validate metrics from the joint test.

[00:13:05] [longer monologue, timestamp jumps] Ethan (SE): A few technical specifics to include in the runbook — exact autoscaler settings (we suggested dropping target CPU by 12%), eviction margin increase, deploying a prefix cold‑start warming job to prepopulate hot keys at morning peaks, and a traffic shaping rule to de‑prioritize batch jobs during high user load windows. We'll also include a canary config: 10% traffic to fallback for 48 hours, metrics to monitor: p50/p95/p99, error rate, retry ratio, and KV miss rate. If any of those exceed thresholds we abort.

[00:14:40] Marta (SRE): Can you share the exact k6 script? We prefer something we can run in our CI.

[00:14:51] Ethan (SE): Yes. We'll push the script to the shared repo and include readme.

[00:15:10] Priya (AE): Security Qs again — David, you asked about audit log granularity. Redwood has request-level audit logs with retention options; longer term Private gives you full control. I'll put the retention and sample log schema in the attachment.

[00:15:36] David (CTO): Great. Also what's the support path if the canary trips? Do we go to Redwood oncall or do you want us to escalate via support portal?

[00:15:48] Priya (AE): For the pilot we'll create a named escalation path — AE/SE oncall plus a dedicated Slack channel to speed triage. We'll include oncall rotations in the runbook.

[00:16:05] Liam (Head of Platform): Any cost estimate for the additional cache reservation and canary traffic? We need numbers for finance.

[00:16:17] Ethan (SE): We'll produce a delta cost sheet — estimate simultaneously: cache reservation ~3% of monthly committed, canary traffic depends on volume but for 10% of user-facing traffic it'll be roughly X in dollars — we'll provide a worked example.

[00:16:45] Marta (SRE): A slightly embarrassing note — we found in our logs a few malformed retry loops from our orchestrator that amplified the surge — we already patched that. That may have been a major amplifier.

[00:17:05] David (CTO): So multiple contributing factors: malformed retries + cache thrash + autoscale tuning. Ok.

[00:17:24] Priya (AE): Recap — immediate: runbook draft, k6 harness, telemetry hooks, share security docs, schedule joint test week of Jan 26, and do a canary redirect. Owners: Ethan for runbook/script, Priya for docs + finance sheet, Marta for traffic profiles.

[00:17:50] Ethan (SE): We'll also prepare a short regression test prompt set so you can validate output quality differences between primary and fallback.

[00:18:10] Marta (SRE): One more ask — can Redwood provide a short list of recommended kernel/quantization profiles if we choose to tune the model? We don't want to accidentally degrade quality.

[00:18:23] Ethan (SE): Sure — we'll include recommended quantization choices and expected quality deltas from our eval bench. Note that some vendor names in those docs got mis-ocr'd on earlier drafts so we'll be careful with naming.

[00:19:05] David (CTO): Anything else on exec comms?

[00:19:12] Priya (AE): We'll prepare the postmortem draft and the 90‑day mitigation roadmap, you review, and David signs off.

[00:19:25] [brief cross talk as attendees check calendars]

[00:20:10] Ethan (SE): Quick note about monitoring: we'll add per-route cost telemetry so you can see token costs by rule and the tradeoff in real time. That should help with the cost/throughput decisions.

[00:20:40] Marta (SRE): That will help. Also please include a sample alert rule — like KV miss rate > 2% for 10 minutes triggers paged alert.

[00:21:00] Ethan (SE): Will do.

[00:21:30] Priya (AE): Ok, last admin — we'll send a summary email in 1 hour with attachments and a proposed slot for the load test. Anything blocking that?

[00:21:45] David (CTO): No blockers.

[00:22:05] Marta (SRE): Not from SRE.

[00:22:20] Liam (Head of Platform): Thanks everyone.

[00:22:30] Priya (AE): Thanks all — quick recap once again and we'll follow up.

[00:22:40] [meeting ends — remaining 30 minutes were used for small breakout with engineers; transcript cuts here but action items captured above.]
questions: Will Dedicated capacity remove the risk of cache thrash fully?
Can Redwood provide the k6 harness and prompt regression set?
How granular are audit logs for Private deployment and KMS integration timeline?
